properties.name: Three genuine internal contracts are declared, and 56 non-seams are named as such
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word 2026-08-27, choosing to work the real candidates over three alternatives after being shown that 56 of the 64 are not seams.

⚠️ A PREDICTION MADE BEFORE THIS WORK WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. This event first stated that declaring these contracts COULD NOT move the seam metric, citing `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet`: couplings come from DEPENDS_ON, contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES, and on this design the two sets were "disjoint by construction". **It moved: 8 of 72 covered became 13 of 72.**

The August measurement was true WHEN TAKEN and its explanation was incomplete. The sets were disjoint because every contract then sat at the SUBSYSTEM boundary while every coupling sat between MODULES — an accident of where contracts had been declared, not a property of the schema. Declaring a contract between two modules that DO carry a DEPENDS_ON edge makes the sets intersect, and five did: detect↔llm, ingest↔llm, ingest↔sanitize, export↔provenance, graph↔provenance.

⭐ SO THE METRIC WAS NEVER STUCK — IT WAS UNREACHABLE FROM WHERE THE CONTRACTS WERE. "Disjoint by construction" reads as a property of the design that no work can change, and it is not; it is a description of a state that this change altered. That distinction matters because the first reading argues for leaving the number alone forever.

🛑 AND ONE OF THE EIGHT STAYED UNCOVERED, CORRECTLY. `cmp:agent`↔`cmp:llm` is still uncovered because BOTH sides PROVIDE `ifc:llm-backend` — agent.rs is an alternative implementation of the trait, not a consumer of llm.rs — so there is no provides/consumes PAIR between them. That is honest modelling producing an uncovered coupling, and it must not be "fixed" by drawing a CONSUMES edge that would assert a relationship the code does not have.

WHY THESE THREE, from the modules' own words rather than from taste:
- `llm.rs` opens *"the one seam between the deterministic core and any LLM"*. It had no Interface node while being the design's most explicitly named boundary. Five modules name `LlmBackend`; `cmp:llm` and `cmp:agent` both PROVIDE it (agent.rs is the ambient-agent ADAPTER, which is why it both provides this and consumes `ifc:ambient-agent`), and detect, ingest and drift consume it.
- `sanitize.rs` opens *"the ingress trust boundary"*, and `req:trust-boundary-at-ingress` is accepted intent. Its error model is the contract: stripping must be SAID OUT LOUD, because a boundary that cleans text silently leaves the reader believing they saw the original.
- `provenance.rs` writes files BESIDE the store that a DIFFERENT VINTAGE of the binary reads. That is a cross-version file-format contract by definition, and six modules read or write it.

WHY NOT THE OTHER TWO. `cmp:graph`↔`cmp:schema` is a compile-time embed of the vocabulary, and `cmp:agent`↔`cmp:nodes` is use of node-type constants. Both are ordinary internal calls, and declaring a contract for them would be the same alarm-on-correct-work that the 56 impl-block pairs represent. Recorded here rather than left silent so the next reader knows they were examined and rejected, not missed.

⚠️ EVERY SPEC WAS FILLED IN, DELIBERATELY. An Interface whose fields are all `unspecified` is a node, not a contract — `seam_report` reports unspecified as UNSTATED rather than as agreement precisely so that cannot pass for one. Medium, paradigm, payload format, operations, payload schema, auth, transport security and error model are set on all three.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: `undeclared_seam` reported 64 uncontracted module pairs. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 against today's code: 56 of the 64 are pairs where BOTH sides are `impl DesignGraph` blocks — one Rust type split across files — and ZERO cross a crate boundary. Only 8 were candidates. Three real contracts are now declared and fully specified: `ifc:llm-backend`, `ifc:ingress-trust-boundary`, `ifc:provenance-sidecar`, each with both sides wired. Module-level seam coverage moved 8/72 → 13/72. Two of the eight (`cmp:graph`↔`cmp:schema`, `cmp:agent`↔`cmp:nodes`) were judged ordinary internal calls; a third (`cmp:agent`↔`cmp:llm`) stays uncovered because both sides PROVIDE the trait rather than one consuming it.
